scores.why: Long QT companion where verdicts come from a fixed drug dataset and the LLM only explains them, checked by a validator; adds genotype- and activity-aware heart-rate limits, recovery tracking and fall detection on the watch.

The Sport & Healthcare deck covers sport (limits by rest, training or sleep, recovery after effort, a coach guide), physical health and access to care (doctor brief, emergency card, SOS); it turns watch and medicine data into decisions. Mental wellbeing is thin.
Offline-first with real flows and a released package, but HarmonyOS-only, a small target group (about 19k people in Poland), and it would need medical-device clearance.
Consistent warm palette, clear verdict sheets, a clean emergency tab and a high-contrast watch alert; the deck has charts and real captures.
About 38k lines in the app, 6.8k on the watch, 7k backend and 5k lines of tests; live web card. NFC and push marked unverified.

scores.why: Faceless, chat-free meetups: the app proposes a plan or pings two compatible people nearby, then a bearing-only compass brings them together; a matching model trained in the repo. The deck itself says it combines known mechanics (happn, Breeze, Timeleft).

Loneliness is framed as a WHO health risk and 16 of 44 activities are sport, but the deck says 'not therapy: no health claims, no health data', there is a Date mode, nothing about access to care beyond support lines, and no health data driving decisions.
One-tap flows and real iOS/Android builds via TestFlight. Network density and safety when meeting strangers are hard; plan show-up rates are still unverified; demo mode relies on simulated users.
Polished Apple-style UI (vibe cards, zone map, plan cards); the deck is a clean 10-slide editorial PDF but text-heavy with few product shots.
Expo app about 13.6k lines, server 4.2k, shared protocol package, ML training and scorer 5.4k, 186 server tests, CI and deploy workflows; the model is trained on synthetic profiles only.

scores.why: Browser-based first-person operating room for a hernia repair with skin that responds to cutting and 17 scored steps; ambitious, but surgical simulators are an established market (Osso VR, Touch Surgery).
Medical education is healthcare-adjacent, but it does not touch sport, users' physical or mental health, access to care, or health data driving decisions.
Free web access suits students, but one module, mouse input, no haptics and a 63 MB download; the site says the steps still need a surgeon's review; dashboard data is seeded.
Photogrammetry operating room, vitals HUD and a polished dark website with a brand book; tissue renders as a flat sheet and in-sim UI is basic.
About 5.5k lines of C# running as a live WebGL build with scoring and a bridge to the site; no tests; website progress is mocked.

calibration_note: Relation to Category decided the order; only Celia uses health data to drive decisions across sport and care. This review ran from the just-mate workspace, so read JustMate's score with that in mind.
